items.title: Housing Needs Assessment Report Findings
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development

Erik Karvinen, Watson & Associates indicated the Housing Needs Assessment provides an assessment of current and future housing needs and strategic recommendations for the Township. He noted the study analyzes economic, demographic and real estate trends to inform future housing demand and policy for the next few decades.

E. Karvinen outlined the population and housing growth trends, suggesting population growth in Centre Wellington has accelerated post 2021, growing by 7% to 34,300 in 2024. He also outlined the existing and future housing needs and provided the study conclusions and recommendations.

E. Karvinen and staff responded to questions regarding temporary agriculture housing, additional residential lots on serviced lands, the need to update the definition of affordable housing in accordance with the new P.P.S., 2024 and update affordable housing targets to align with affordable housing needs, and the next steps.

items.title: Corporate Climate Action Plan Terms of Reference
notes: Report from M. Tamlyn, Climate Change Coordinator
M. Tamlyn, Climate Change Coordinator outlined the primary objectives of the corporate climate action plan, including:
- Establishing a baseline of current GHG emissions
- Conducting a climate risk assessment for key infrastructure and services
- Identifying priorities, pathways, and timelines for implementing effective mitigation and adaptation strategies
- Setting ambitious but achievable targets
- Integrating climate considerations into municipal business processes;
and
- Identifying and secure climate budget allocation and funding sources He outlined the pathways, priorities and targets, the deliverables and the expected project completion by Q2 of 2026.
Mayor Watters called for a 7 minute break.

items.title: Operations Centre - Solar Panel Update
notes: Report from M. Tamlyn, Climate Change Coordinator

M. Tamlyn, Climate Change Coordinator provided an overview of the report, including the environmental and financial benefits of solar. He indicated after review, a net-metered rooftop system is considered the preferred choice. He suggested this design utilizes existing infrastructure, can accommodate energy needs throughout the year, and provides the most significant net return and GHG reduction.

items.title: Intersection Improvement Recommendations
notes: Report from A. Gilmore, Manager of Engineering

Adam Gilmore, Manager of Engineering provided an overview of the report, indicating the Township's Active Transportation and Mobility Plan has identified needs for safety and crossing improvements at several intersections, noting that intersections located along school routes should be prioritized.
The four locations noted as high priority for improvement are:
1. The intersection of Beatty Line, Sideroad 18, and Farley Road in Fergus;
2. The intersection of Beatty Line, Millage Lane, and Elliot Avenue East in Fergus;
3. The intersection of Gartshore Street, Middleton Avenue, and Forfar Street East in Fergus; and,
4. The intersection of David Street and Irvine Street in Elora.

items.title: Parks and Recreation Plan - Final Approval
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services provided an overview of the report, indicating the final report includes the following:
- Engagement Report: A summary of community input received, highlighting themes and key concerns raised by participants.
- Needs Assessment: An extensive review identifying the existing opportunities and needs regarding parks and recreation across the Township, projecting future requirements.
- Parks Plan: A framework categorizing parks and providing a roadmap for future parkland dedication and development, including a draft Parkland Dedication Bylaw for Council’s future consideration.
- Parks and Recreation Plan: Defined themes with actionable recommendations focusing on partnerships, facility development, programming, and outdoor spaces.
Staff responded to questions regarding the next steps and budget implications.
